acceleron.basis: Firm's listing and Wikipedia: IPO 2013, acquired by Merck (closed 2021-11-19); Bessemer's 2007 entry came after the 2003 Series A and a Series B (the 2007 Series C), read from memory of the round, not a page in hand.

acorn-cardiovascular.basis: CorCap heart-device maker that failed FDA approval and wound down around 2010 to 2011 (Inquirer 2010-12-01 headline on its critical condition); no source names the 1999 round Bessemer entered.

aivar.basis: Firm's own post of 2026-01-08: Bessemer invests in Aivar's $4.6M seed round (led by Sorin per the Indian press); the company's contact page lists Coimbatore as HQ.

aiwyn.basis: Bessemer entered in the $113M round it led with KKR (2024-12-19, Business Wire and TechCrunch); the round carries no series letter and no valuation, total raised $127M, so it reads Growth by scale and no $1B mark exists; TechCrunch places the company in Charlotte.

ansible-health.basis: Company site is live (copyright 2025, seeing patients in all states); the firm lists a 2021 investment with no round word and no press names the round; Mountain View from the company's published research affiliation.

bettermode.basis: BetaKit 2021-06-29: Bessemer and CRV led Toronto-based Tribe's $7.5M seed, closed November 2020; Tribe renamed itself Bettermode and still operates (CX Today 2026-08).

businessland.basis: Firm's archive says Brownstein 'participated in the company's early rounds' (no round named), IPO 1983; the retailer was bought by JWP (UPI 1991-08-05: 'JWP completes acquisition of Businessland'); San Jose from memory.

cambly.basis: Firm lists a 2018 investment; TechCrunch (2023) says Cambly reached profitability before its Series A, and the funding histories date that $15M Series A to June 2018, so the 2018 entry is the Series A; no $1B priced event found.

cloudinary.basis: Wikipedia: Bessemer's 2015 investment was a secondary (Growth); Blackstone's 2022 secondary purchase valued the company at $2B (a priced transaction, now a stale mark); HQ moved to San Jose in 2024.

comanage.basis: Telecom provisioning software company at 12330 Perry Highway, Wexford PA; a web search returned an acquisition in 2005 (acquirer not confirmed in a page I read, Syndesis from memory); no source names the 1999 round.

counterpane.basis: Firm's own 2008 history page: Schneier turned to David Cowan 'to lead the Series A round' (invest date 1999-08-05); acquired by BT on 2006-10-25 (firm's listing and Wikipedia); Mountain View was its last HQ, from memory.

datahub.basis: Firm's post of 2025-05-21: Bessemer leads DataHub's $35M Series B, and both the site and the archive give 2025 as the investment year, so the Series B is the entry; the company's own page says it is headquartered in Palo Alto; no $1B priced round found (total raised about $65M).

diogenes.basis: Listed 2003 to 2004 only; a 2003 ITWeb release calls Diogenes a US developer of business transaction network software (product iMercury), nothing found on its city, its rounds or its fate.

docutap.basis: Firm's listing: acquired by Warburg Pincus in 2016 (merged with Practice Velocity into Experity in 2019, Argus Leader); Bessemer's 2013-04 investment was the bootstrapped company's first outside money and no source I read gives it a round name.

doubledutch.basis: Firm's listing: acquired by Cvent in June 2019; Bessemer led the $10.5M round of autumn 2013 (invest date 2013-09-09), which came after the company's seed and Series A (a Series B or C), named from memory rather than a page read in this pass.

eliseai.basis: TechCrunch 2026-09-29: $350M round led by a16z and Bessemer at a $4B valuation; the firm's own post of 2025-08-20 says Bessemer 'joins EliseAI's $250M Series E', its entry.

exp-systems.basis: EXP.com, a dot-com era expert-advice marketplace that raised a $33M third round in 2000 and left the firm's list after 2002; I found no page stating its end or its city (probably shut down in 2001 to 2002, not confirmed).

fandom.basis: Wikipedia: Wikia's first venture round was $4M from Bessemer and First Round in 2006 (invest date 2006-01-20), followed by Amazon's Series B, so the entry is the Series A; acquired in February 2018 by TPG-backed Jon Miller; HQ at 130 Sutter Street, San Francisco.

finmark.basis: Firm's listing: acquired by Bill.com in November 2022; Bessemer entered in 2020, the year the company was founded and went through YC, in its seed financing (the $5M seed reported in January 2021), named from memory.

graph-ai.basis: Firm's post of 2025-10-16: Bessemer leads Graph AI's seed round ($3M per the Indian press); a $13.3M Series A followed in September 2026; the company's contact page gives Pleasanton, California as its head office with a second office in Hyderabad.

hunters.basis: Press shows a $15M Series A in June 2020 and a $68M Series C in January 2022; Bessemer's 2021 entry is the Series B it led in between (from memory); the company's site is live in 2026 and no $1B priced round turned up in the news check.

inrisk.basis: Firm's post of 2025-01-14: 'Bessemer Venture Partners leads Inrisk's Seed fundraise'; a $27M Series A followed on 2026-08-05; Inc42 calls the company GIFT City-based (Gandhinagar), another outlet says Ahmedabad.

itc-deltacom.basis: Wikipedia: acquired by EarthLink in December 2010 after a 2002 bankruptcy; the firm's 2000 listing gives only the year 1996 and a ticker, no round; Huntsville, Alabama was its last HQ, from memory.

jasper.basis: Firm's own post of 2022-10-18: Bessemer's growth practice 'joins the $125 million Series A of Jasper ... at a $1.5 billion valuation'; the 2023 internal valuation cut was not a priced event, so the mark stands, now stale.

legora.basis: Wikipedia: the $550M round of March 2026 valued Legora at $5.55B (press puts the April 2026 extension at $5.6B post-money; the $8.5B to $10B talks are only reported); the firm's post of 2025-10-30 says Bessemer leads the $150M Series C, its 2025 entry.

main-street-hub.basis: Firm's listing: acquired by GoDaddy in 2018 (Business Journals: a $125M deal); Bessemer entered in 2013 by leading the $14M Series B, named from memory rather than a page read in this pass.

maintainx.basis: Autodesk completed its acquisition of MaintainX in August 2026 (ARC Advisory 2026-08-18, Autodesk's Q2 call; the firm's site gives 2026-08-03); Bessemer entered in 2021 by leading the Series B and co-led the 2025 Series D.

multiflow-computers.basis: Wikipedia: Multiflow closed its first venture round in January 1985 and ceased operations in 1990; the firm's list gives only the year 1985, so the round Bessemer entered is not named.

nitrous-io.basis: Bessemer's 2012-08-09 investment was the roughly $1M seed of Action.IO (later Nitrous.IO), followed by the Series A it led in 2013; the service shut down in November 2016; all from memory, no page read in this pass.

okera.basis: Firm's listing and TechCrunch 2023-05-03: acquired by Databricks in May 2023; Bessemer's 2017-11-13 investment is the $12M Series A it led (announced March 2018), the seed having been Felicis's, from memory.

pipedrive.basis: Wikipedia: the $9M Series A of 2015 was led by Bessemer (invest date 2015-04-29); Vista took a majority stake in November 2020 at about $1.5B, which the firm records as an acquisition; Wikipedia gives New York as the HQ (founded in Tallinn, where most staff sit).

productboard.basis: Wikipedia: the $125M Series D of February 2022 valued the company at $1.725B (stale; a 30% layoff in April 2026 but no lower priced event); Bessemer entered in 2019 by leading the Series B, after Kleiner Perkins's Series A, from memory.

pure-networks.basis: Firm's listing: acquired by Cisco in 2008; Bessemer's 2005-12-21 investment was, from memory, the $10M Series B it led, not confirmed on a page in this pass.

quantopian.basis: Wikipedia: Quantopian announced its shutdown in November 2020 and the team moved to Robinhood, which did not buy the company (acqui-hire rule: the company's own fate decides); Bessemer led the $15M round of October 2014 (Finovate), the Series B after Spark's seed and Khosla's Series A.

quidsi-fka-diapers-com.basis: Wikipedia and the firm's listing: Amazon bought Quidsi for $545M (announced 2010-11-08, closed 2011); Bessemer's 2007-11-07 investment was, from memory, the Series B after an earlier round from MentorTech and BEV, not confirmed on a page in this pass.

recurrency.basis: Firm's post of 2023-02-02: Kent Bennett 'committed to lead Recurrency's seed round' (2021), then Bessemer led the $22M Series A; YC's directory lists the company as active in San Francisco.

reputation.basis: Wikipedia: Reputation (formerly ReputationDefender) is headquartered in San Ramon and still private; the firm gives 2009-04-17 as its investment date but no source I read names that round (probably the Series B), and no $1B priced round is on record.

revenuebase.basis: The company's first Form D (filed 2022-11-23, $4M, Kent Bennett a director) is a seed-size first round for a company founded in 2021, but no source names it; the company's own FAQ says it is headquartered in Waltham (the Form D address was Newtonville).

rosebud.basis: TechCrunch 2025-06-04: 'The seed round was led by Bessemer Venture Partners' ($6M); the company's own about page says the team is based in Santa Monica.

servicetitan.basis: Firm's own memo of 2015-03-15 recommends investing '$17M in the $18M series A financing'; listed on Nasdaq since December 2024 (TTAN), market cap $6.62B as of 2026-10-06 on StockAnalysis.

stratoscale.basis: Calcalist and Globes, December 2019: Stratoscale shut down and laid off its staff; Haaretz 2013-10-29 reports the $10M first round (Battery and Bessemer, invest date 2013-09-30), the Series A by name from memory; Wikipedia places the HQ in Herzliya.

streambase.basis: Firm's archive: acquired by TIBCO in 2013; it listed the company as Grassy Brook from 2003-07-24, the start-up's first financing (the Series A with Accel, from memory, not confirmed on a page); the company's 2012 Form D gives 181 Spring Street, Lexington.

travcorps.basis: Firm's archive: Bessemer 'invested in its first institutional round in 1995' (no round name, so no label) and the company merged with Cross Country Staffing in 1999; Malden, Massachusetts from memory.

voxel51.basis: Firm's post of 2024-05-16: Bessemer leads the $30M Series B, its 2024 entry (the 2022 Series A was Drive Capital's); no later priced round or sale in the news check; Ann Arbor from memory.

way-systems.basis: The company's 2009 Form D gives 200 Unicorn Park, Woburn; it was bought by VeriFone in September 2010 (from memory, not confirmed on a page); no source names the 2005 round Bessemer entered (probably a Series B).

worldtalk.basis: Firm's archive: Cowan 'led several rounds in Worldtalk, starting in 1993' (no round named), IPO 1996, acquired by Tumbleweed in January 2000; Wikipedia gives Santa Clara as the HQ.

zany-brainy.basis: Wikipedia: Chapter 11 on 2001-05-15 and its assets sold to Right Start later that year (an asset sale out of insolvency reads acquired); the successor FAO liquidated the chain in December 2003; the firm lists only the year 1995; King of Prussia from memory.

zapier.basis: TechCrunch 2012-10-31: Zapier raises a $1.2M seed round from Bessemer, DFJ and others (invest date 2012-09-07); the 2021 secondary sale to Sequoia and Steadfast valued the company at $5B (Wikipedia, Forbes 2021-03-08), a stale mark with nothing priced since.
